# SurveyBeat

Cloudflare-only Effect app. One Durable Object per Organization is the system of record; D1 holds only the global index and auth/email bookkeeping, never survey content. Two Workers serve the app/API (`MainWorker`) and the answer page's submission path (`SubmissionWorker`).

Read `SPEC.md` (authoritative spec), `GLOSSARY.md` (domain vocabulary), and `docs/adr/` (binding decisions) before changing behavior. `docs/infra.md` covers stages, WorkOS sign-in, email, and observability.

## Ground rules

- Use glossary terms exactly: Pulse (not Survey), Person (not User), Round (not instance), Submission (not Response). Do not drift to the "avoid" synonyms.
- If a change contradicts an ADR, say so and add a new ADR under `docs/adr/`; never silently override one.
- Issues and specs live in GitHub issues (`gh`); conventions are in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`. Commit subjects name the release slice, e.g. `R1 03: ...`.
- Privacy invariants are release blockers (SPEC §7): anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time (ADR 0005), comments are redacted at store time (ADR 0009), and every shown aggregate obeys the minimum group size (ADR 0004).

## Commands (from the repo root)

Node 24 (`.node-version`) and pnpm 12.18.0 are pinned.

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm typecheck          # tsc -b with project references
pnpm typecheck:effect   # @effect/tsgo diagnostics; CI runs this first
pnpm lint               # oxlint --type-aware
pnpm format             # oxfmt; CI runs format:check
pnpm test               # Vitest "unit" project only
pnpm test:privacy       # Vitest "privacy" project only; NOT part of pnpm test
pnpm test <path>        # one file, e.g. pnpm test packages/domain/src/people/SignIn.test.ts
pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web build
```

CI runs `typecheck:effect`, `typecheck`, `format:check`, `lint`, `test`, then the web build; the privacy suite is a separate required job. There is no root `dev` script: `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/web dev` serves the UI only, and the app calls the API at `window.location.origin`. Exercise sign-in and end-to-end flows on a deployed stage.

## Layout and boundaries

- `packages/domain` — Effect schemas and services by concept (`people/`, `email/`); depends only on `effect`.
- `packages/api` — the `HttpApi` declaration shared by the Worker and the typed web client; depends on `domain`.
- `packages/cloudflare` — all Cloudflare adapters plus the `MainWorker` and `SubmissionWorker` entries; the only package that touches the Alchemy runtime.
- `apps/web` — one Vite project with two entries: the Foldkit app (`index.html`) and the plain-TypeScript answer page (`answer.html`).
- `packages/emails` — React Email templates and rendering. `packages/testing` — privacy harness. `infra` — Alchemy stack, scripts, Playwright e2e, privacy sweep. `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat` — local lint rules.

## Toolchain traps

- Effect is 4.1.2, not 3.x. Import from `effect/Effect`, `effect/Schema`, `effect/http-api`, `effect/http/...`; there is no `@effect/platform` v3-style API here. Copy the import style from neighboring files.
- TypeScript 7 (native compiler) with `tsc -b`. A new package needs its own `tsconfig.json` and an entry in the root `tsconfig.json` references.
- Stricter than defaults: `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `verbatimModuleSyntax` (use `import type`), and relative imports carry explicit `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Lint bans `any` and type assertions (`as Foo`) outside `*.test.ts` (`consistent-type-assertions: never`). Decode with Effect Schema or use typed helpers instead.
- All user-facing text comes from `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts` or `packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts`; `no-literal-ui-text` fails otherwise. HTML shells must hold no visible text and an empty `<title>` (asserted in `messages.test.ts`). Plurals use `<base>.one`/`.other`.
- The lint plugin enforces the boundaries: `domain`/`api` may not import `cloudflare:*`, Alchemy, or Foldkit, and `apps/web/src/answer/**` may not import React, Base UI, Foldkit, or the HttpApi client.
- Keep the answer entry plain TypeScript within its budget (JS ≤ 10 KB gzip critical path, CSS ≤ 2 KB inline, HTML ≤ 8 KB); no framework, per ADR 0008.

## Tests

- Tests are colocated `*.test.ts`. A privacy test must be named `*.privacy.test.ts` or CI never runs it.
- Use `@effect/vitest` (`it.effect` for Effect programs).
- Adapter tests use `@alchemy.run/test`'s `Test.make({ dev: true })` against local workerd and are slow (deploy timeouts up to 240 s); run the single file you need.
- A new API endpoint must be classified in `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts` or the package will not typecheck; `registry.privacy.test.ts` checks the runtime declaration too.
- End-to-end tests run only against a deployed stage: `E2E_BASE_URL=https://pr-<n>.app.surveybeat.app pnpm test:e2e` (install Chromium once with `pnpm --filter @surveybeat/infra exec playwright install chromium`).

## Infra

- Every Cloudflare resource is declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; no dashboard edits, no wrangler config.
- Run Alchemy from the repo root: the Organization DO migrations path (`packages/cloudflare/migrations`) is relative to the working directory. Build the web app first; the Main Worker serves `apps/web/dist`.
- `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-<name>` needs `WORKOS_API_KEY` and `WORKOS_CLIENT_ID` in the environment. Who may create an Organization is `infra/org-creation-allowlist.yaml`, per stage.
- Non-production stages never send real email; sends are recorded in D1's `captured_email`. Only `production` sends.
- The Submission Worker must keep every observability channel off. `pnpm check:observability --stage <stage>` reads the deployed settings back; the canary sweep proves no logs are kept. Stage scripts need `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`.
- New SQL migrations: numbered files in `packages/cloudflare/migrations` (Durable Object) or `packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations` (D1).

- [Cloudflare cf CLI](cloudflare-cf-cli.md) — authenticated cf CLI for SurveyBeat's Cloudflare account; discover commands with cf cli search
- [Wayfinder: always push and merge](wayfinder-always-push-merge.md) — push and squash-merge each resolved ticket's branch without asking

## Goal
An Organization admin can turn AI processing on, and the Organization Durable Object has a client that can call the model exactly as ADR 0015 allows, and no other way.

## Acceptance criteria
- Organization setting `aiProcessing` (off by default) in the Organization Durable Object, with an Organization admin toggle on the Settings screen that explains what is sent, to whom (OpenRouter, Google Cloud or AWS in the EU), and that nothing is kept.
- While it is on, the answer page and the Invitation and Reminder emails state that redacted comments are processed by an AI service in the EU that keeps nothing (catalog copy).
- An `AiClient` service (domain interface, Cloudflare adapter) that POSTs to OpenRouter Chat Completions with the exact request shape of ADR 0015: `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5`, `provider.zdr: true`, `only`/`order` = `google-vertex/europe`, `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`, `allow_fallbacks: false`, `data_collection: deny`, strict `json_schema`, capped `max_tokens`, low reasoning effort. Key from a Worker secret `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`; timeout; retries on 408/429/502/503 honouring `Retry-After`.
- Response and error bodies are never logged (moderation errors can echo comment text).
- Input is typed so only redacted comment text, Question text, Dimension scores and changes, and redacted Action titles can be passed; no Person, name, id, or time fits the type.

## Tests
- A unit test asserts the request body above byte for byte and that no fallback is possible.
- A privacy test that the input type rejects a Person id or name.
- A fake `AiClient` layer for later slices.

## Follows
ADR 0015, ADR 0009

## Context

Planned on the [Wayfinder map](https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/issues/85). Use `GLOSSARY.md` terms throughout. ADRs are in `docs/adr/`; research in `docs/research/`.
# Comment themes use Claude Haiku 5.5 through OpenRouter, with zero data retention, in the EU, switched on per Organization

Release 2's AI features (comment themes and the AI part of the discussion guide) call `anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5` through OpenRouter. Every request sets `provider.zdr: true`, is pinned to the two zero-data-retention endpoints that run in the EU (`google-vertex/europe`, then `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1`), and allows no fallback. If neither endpoint can serve the request, it fails and is retried later; it never leaves the EU or goes to an endpoint that keeps data. This replaces SPEC §10 question 4's default (Workers AI only), chosen by the product owner on 2026-11-10 (map #85).

**What is sent:** only comment text that rule-based redaction has already processed (ADR 0009), and the Question text. Never a name, a Person id, a Membership, a Round id, a Team or Organization name, a time, or anything that links a comment to a Submission (ADR 0005). The Organization Durable Object makes the call with a key held as a Worker secret, a timeout, and retries that honour `Retry-After`. Response and error bodies are never logged, because a provider's moderation error can echo comment text.

**Off by default.** An Organization admin turns AI processing on for the Organization. While it is off, nothing is sent and the AI features do not appear. While it is on, the answer page and the Invitation say plainly that redacted comments are processed by an AI service in the EU that keeps nothing.

**Request shape** (Chat Completions):

```json
{
  "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5",
  "provider": {
    "zdr": true,
    "only": ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"],
    "order": ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"],
    "allow_fallbacks": false,
    "data_collection": "deny"
  },
  "response_format": { "type": "json_schema", "json_schema": { "strict": true } },
  "max_tokens": 2000
}
```

The OpenRouter account also has prompt and output logging off, "use of inputs/outputs" off, and a dedicated key whose guardrail allows only this model, enforces ZDR, and caps spend.

## Considered options

- **`meta/muse-ember`** (the first choice): no zero-retention endpoint exists. Meta, its only host, keeps prompts for 30 days, is not on EU routing, and its own terms don't say whether this model is trained on. Rejected: members' words would sit with a US provider for 30 days ([research note](../research/openrouter-muse-ember.md)).
- **`openai/gpt-6-luna`:** same price, zero retention only through Azure. Viable, but Haiku 5.5 has EU zero-retention endpoints with strict JSON-schema output.
- **`meta/muse-spark-open`:** zero retention on several hosts, but about 9× the price, with no advantage over Haiku 5.5.
- **Workers AI** (SPEC's default): keeps everything inside Cloudflare, but the product owner chose OpenRouter.

## Consequences

- Cost is about $0.0015 per Round ($0.10 per million input and $0.50 per million output tokens; one call of about 2,000 input and 2,500 output tokens), an estimate until a real call measures it.
- OpenRouter is a sub-processor (its DPA is part of its terms), and so are Google Cloud or AWS for the model call. Customer-facing privacy pages must name them.
- OpenRouter's account and abuse-monitoring metadata may be processed in the US even when the model call runs in the EU. Comment text is not part of that metadata under ZDR.
- If either EU endpoint drops ZDR or leaves OpenRouter, requests fail closed rather than going elsewhere. A test asserts the request body above.

Verdict: no BLOCKERs. There is one MAJOR deploy risk (item 6, unverified) and a few MINORs. `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm lint` are clean. The targeted run of 12 test files (`packages/domain/src/ai`, `packages/cloudflare/src/ai`, `packages/domain/src/people`, `apps/web`) passed 266 of 266. I did not run `pnpm typecheck:effect`, `pnpm test:privacy` or the deploy path.

**MAJOR (unverified)**

- **Empty `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` default may break deploys.** The location is `packages/cloudflare/src/MainWorker.ts:129`, where the env entry is `Config.Redacted("OPENROUTER_API_KEY").pipe(Config.withDefault(Redacted.make("")))`.
  - **Failure scenario:** a stage with no secret, such as a fork PR or a personal `dev-*` stage, is deployed. The deploy then binds a Worker secret with an empty value. Cloudflare's secret APIs, as I recall, reject an empty `secret_text` (`wrangler secret put` does).
  - **Related case:** the workflows pass `${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}`. When the repository secret is missing, GitHub sets the variable to an empty string. That is "present but empty", not "missing".
  - **Why I'm unsure:** I could not verify Alchemy's behaviour here. The `localTestSecrets.ts` default only proves the local workerd path works.
  - **Fix:** spread the binding in only when the value is non-empty (`...(key === "" ? {} : { OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ... })`), and read it in the adapter with `Config.option`. Alternatively, confirm with one `pnpm infra:deploy --stage dev-x` run without the secret.
  - **Safe part:** `makeOpenRouterAiClient` itself is safe either way. A missing or empty key returns `AiNotConfigured` with no fetch, and a test covers both cases.

**MINOR**

1. **Unconsumed response bodies on retried statuses.** In `packages/cloudflare/src/ai/OpenRouterAiClient.ts`, the loop `continue`s on 408/429/502/503 without cancelling the body. The same applies to the `AiRejected` return. Workers hold the connection until the body is consumed or cancelled, so a retry storm can stall on the connection limit.
   - **Fix:** call `response.body?.cancel()` in those branches. That does not read the body, so the privacy rule still holds.
2. **Empty PATCH body is accepted.** `packages/api/src/index.ts:173` makes both fields optional, so `{}` returns success and writes a no-op `SettingsUpdated`. Nothing is flipped by accident, and the SQL always writes both columns from the merged state. A `minimumGroupSize`-only PATCH keeps `aiProcessing`, and the reverse holds too, as `Directory.test.ts` verifies.
   - **Fix:** reject an empty payload with a schema filter, or accept the no-op deliberately.
3. **Timeout and body-read failures.** `AbortSignal.timeout` also covers the body read. A `response.json()` failure from an abort on a 2xx reply becomes `AiRejected(200)` rather than a retryable timeout. That is rare and fails closed.
4. **`Retry-After` as an HTTP-date** falls back to exponential backoff. `Retry-After: 0` retries immediately. Both are still bounded at 4 attempts and at most 30 s per wait.
5. **Secret declaration location.** The issue says the secret is "declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`". It is declared in `MainWorker.ts`, the same place as `WORKOS_*`, and `docs/infra.md` documents it. This is fine as long as that is the project's convention.

**Requested checks**

1. **Request body: clean.** `openRouterRequestBody` is the only builder and hard-types `zdr: true`, `allow_fallbacks: false` and `data_collection: "deny"`. The `only` and `order` arrays come from one constant. The test compares byte for byte against the ADR. The extras beyond the ADR block (`reasoning.effort: "low"`, `messages`, schema name) are as the issue requires.
2. **Bodies, logging, retries: clean.** Error bodies are never read, a test proves it with throwing body methods, and nothing logs. The retry loop is capped at 4 attempts, with waits of 1, 2 and 4 seconds or `Retry-After` capped at 30 s. A single attempt is 60 s, so the worst case is about 5.5 minutes.
3. **API key leak: clean.** The key is `Redacted` until the header is built. Errors carry only `status` and `reason`. Test output shows only a fake key.
4. **AiInput typing: clean.** Strict `Struct`s plus `@ts-expect-error` tests confirm that ids, names and plain strings are rejected, and `tsc` enforces them. The `RedactedText` brand can still be minted with `RedactedText.make(anyString)`. That is inherent to branding and is documented.
5. **Admin-only and migration: clean.** `UpdateSettings` still goes through `can(... "organization.updateSettings")`, and there is a Forbidden test for non-admins. The migration `0011_ai_processing.sql` is numbered correctly, with `NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and a CHECK. SQLite accepts that `ADD COLUMN` on existing rows. The row decode uses `=== 1`.
7. **PATCH regression: clean apart from MINOR 2.** The web `UpdateSettings` still sends only `minimumGroupSize`, and the new `UpdateAiProcessing` sends only `aiProcessing`.
8. **Test quality: good.** The tests assert behaviour: byte-for-byte body, retries and waits, no body read, and a scene test for the toggle. I found no weakened tests, and the fixtures were only extended with `aiProcessing: false`.
9. **Conventions: clean.** The new code has no `as` outside tests, the UI copy is in the catalog, and the Effect 4 style matches neighbouring files.
